dedupe_keys.name: national digital twin programme integration architecture uk open source code

description: The UK National Digital Twin Programme publishes an open-source ecosystem for secure, federated data sharing between digital twins. Its Integration Architecture defines how integration architecture nodes, management nodes and the node network interoperate, with principles, standards and technical guidelines for data sharing, security and interoperability, and a video guide shows how to deploy and configure an IA node with Helm charts in a local Kubernetes environment. Data interoperability rests on the Information Exchange Standard (IES). All code is on GitHub in public repositories and a container registry, following a GitFlow branching model; code contributions are limited to approved suppliers, but anyone can report issues and suggest documentation changes. The programme's demonstrators include NOVA (renewable generation and storage), IRIS (home retrofit), LISA (incident response), SALUS (multi-agency crisis response) and VISTA (cascading asset failures). Source code is released under the Apache License 2.0 and documentation under the Open Government Licence v3.0, and use is free. Caveats: the architecture is still evolving and public pull requests are not accepted. Coverage is the United Kingdom. It supports interdependency and cascading failure analysis across infrastructure operators by federating their data; related records are the CReDo climate resilience demonstrator and the Dutch socio-technical interdependencies dataset.
